https://www.ispreview.co.uk/index.php/20.summary: The City of London Corporation has selected Roc Technologies to deliver a new end‑to‑end network that includes AI‑driven wireless capabilities. The AI is used to optimise wireless performance and ensure high‑availability connectivity for public services, improving network efficiency across the city.

Octaplus has launched an AI‑powered support system called Ask Octa AI, a chatbot/virtual assistant that handles customer queries and troubleshooting, aiming to improve the customer experience and reduce support workload.

Ofcom is deploying an unidentified third‑party monitoring tool that appears to use AI to track VPN usage across the UK. The system aims to detect and deter circumvention of the Online Safety Act’s censorship provisions, thereby enforcing government policy on internet content. This represents a security-focused application of AI in regulatory monitoring.

BT has partnered with CrowdStrike to launch an AI‑powered antivirus service called Business Antivirus Detect and Respond (BADR) for small UK businesses. The solution uses AI to proactively detect and respond to threats before they become breaches, enhancing security for its small‑business customers.

Cornerstone has adopted Vyntelligence’s Agentic Video Intelligence AI platform to accelerate the deployment of new masts across the UK, reducing rollout time and cutting costs. The AI-driven video analysis helps identify optimal sites and streamline construction, improving efficiency for the network operator.
Gigaclear has adopted Vyntelligence's AI video technology to streamline customer installation journeys, reducing unnecessary work and improving the overall customer experience.

Ulster University researchers use AI to develop a new massive MIMO (ma‑MIMO) technology for 6G, aiming to make future mobile broadband networks faster, smarter, and more energy‑efficient. The AI‑driven design enhances signal processing and antenna array efficiency, potentially boosting network performance and reducing power consumption. This advancement could accelerate 6G deployment and improve user experience.

Virgin Media O2 has launched Lumi AI, an AI-powered tool designed to enhance customer service by enabling agents to deliver faster, more effective, and personalized support. The system uses AI to streamline interactions and improve response times, aiming to boost customer satisfaction and operational efficiency. This initiative positions VMO2 as a leader in AI-driven customer experience within the UK telecom market.

TalkTalk has adopted NICE’s CXone Mpower, an AI‑powered customer service automation platform, to enhance its customer support capabilities and move closer to becoming the UK’s most recommended Wi‑Fi provider. The platform automates ticket handling and self‑service interactions, aiming to improve response times and customer satisfaction.

O2 (Virgin Media) has deployed Hiya’s AI‑powered Call Defence service to flag scam and spam calls. The system has identified over 150 million suspected fraud calls, rising to more than 50 million per month, helping protect customers from nuisance and fraudulent calls.

Vodafone UK and Ericsson trial AI and ML powered software solutions that cut daily power consumption of 5G radio units by 33%, improving energy efficiency and reducing operational costs. The trials demonstrate how AI can optimize network energy usage in real-world deployments.
The article reports that O2 (Virgin Media O2) will invest £700m in network upgrades, including increased automation via AI, but does not detail any specific AI applications.

The UK Spectrum Policy Forum recommends that Ofcom adopt AI technologies to improve spectrum management, enabling more efficient allocation and use of the finite wireless radio spectrum. AI would help predict demand, optimize allocation, and reduce interference, supporting the telecom sector's growth.

The system helps protect customers from fraud and frees up resources, demonstrating a proactive approach to fraud prevention.

The report from EY and Liberty Global calls for strategic AI adoption in the UK telco sector to achieve major sustainability gains over the next decade, though specific implementations are not detailed.

BT is deploying AI-powered virtual assistants and chatbots to handle up to 60,000 customer conversations per week, aiming to streamline support processes and enhance the customer experience. The use of AI-based systems in customer support is positioned as a significant improvement over traditional methods.

O2 has integrated Hiya’s AI‑powered scam call detection service into its network, offering customers a free tool that identifies and blocks fraud and nuisance calls. The deployment helps protect users from scams and enhances call quality, positioning O2 as a leader in customer protection.
